APPLICATION 04 / REMOVE

Treat sediment, access and discharge as one problem.

For submerged sumps, a viable dredging system connects the vehicle to a pump, conveyance route and sediment-treatment plan.

Applications / Robotic sump cleaning & confined-space dredging

Who this is for

Hydropower maintenance teams and contractors managing compatible submerged sumps.

Project inputs

  • Sump drawing, access opening and depth
  • Sediment thickness, solids content and particle size
  • Debris and fiber information
  • Lift, discharge route and treatment constraints
Build a project brief
01

Characterize what needs to move

Provide sediment depth, solids content, particle-size distribution, fibers and hard debris. These determine suction, blockage and treatment requirements more directly than the vehicle name.

02

Check access and recovery

Review the opening size, vehicle clearance, water depth, wall shape and lifting arrangement. A confined-space task needs a recovery plan that remains workable if mobility or suction is lost.

03

Calculate the complete conveyance duty

Specify pipe diameter and route, horizontal distance, lift and discharge point. The pump-and-pipe combination must be assessed with the expected sediment, not clean-water assumptions alone.

04

Distinguish treatment capacity from removal productivity

The AD-100 brochure lists 5 m³/h for its accompanying mud-water separation equipment. It does not establish how much net sediment the robot removes per hour.

05

Define measurement and material handling

Agree how recovered material is measured, where separated solids go, how water is treated and which site permissions apply. Ask for a representative sediment test and an acceptance method.

BEFORE YOU SPECIFY

Questions worth resolving.

Is AD-100 suitable for any tank?

No. Access, geometry, material and operating conditions need review. The cited use is a hydropower sump application, not proof for every industrial vessel.

Is 5 m³/h the dredging rate?

No. It is the brochure’s capacity for supporting mud-water separation equipment. Net removal productivity needs a separate measured basis.
